unverified.detail: No orders exist on this account to look up amend history for -- needs a real order_id.

spec.description:
Retrieve an audit trail of amend transactions on the specified order. The list is ordered by ascending amend timestamp; the first entry contains the original order parameters and has `amend_type` of `original`.

**API Key Permissions Required:** `Orders and trades - Query open orders & trades` or `Orders and trades - Query closed orders & trades`, depending on the status of the order.

order_id.description: The Kraken order identifier for the amended order.

rebase_multiplier.description: Optional parameter for viewing xstocks data. `rebased` displays in terms of underlying equity, `base` displays in terms of SPV tokens.

response.title: OrderAmendsFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

error.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

result.title: OrderAmends
result.description: The amend transaction history for one order.

count.description: Total count of new and amend transactions (including the original order).

amends.description: Amend transactions, ordered by ascending amend timestamp.

amend_type.description: The type of amend transaction: `original` (original order values on order entry), `user` (user-requested amendment), or `restated` (engine order maintenance amendment).

order_qty.description: Order quantity in terms of the base asset.

display_qty.description: The quantity shown in the book for iceberg orders.

remaining_qty.description: Remaining un-traded quantity on the order.

limit_price.description: The limit price restriction on the order.

trigger_price.description: The trigger price on trigger order types.

reason.description: Description of the reason for this amend.

post_only.description: Indicates if the transaction was restricted from taking liquidity.

timestamp.description: The UNIX timestamp for the amend transaction, in nanosecond precision.

notes: Upstream's OpenAPI `required` array lists `txid` (copied from a sibling operation), but the actual field is `order_id`, which the doc page and example both confirm is required. Corrected here to `required: ["order_id"]`. No pagination block: `count` is a plain total, not paired with any offset/limit parameter -- the whole amend history is returned in one response.

`amends[].timestamp` declares `format: "epoch-nanos"` (rule 3): the field's own description states nanosecond precision (an integer UNIX timestamp in nanoseconds), which is now a supported format -- renders to the client core's `TimestampNanos` (`typed_core.times.EpochConverter.nanoseconds()`).
